- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or neutral (0.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 3–7 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract underestimation.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.0 values, model may be overfitting to recent noise; apply a 5–10% smoothing filter to reduce volatility amplification.
